access_evidence: probe openalex_works_search: HTTP 200 with a compound filter (raw_affiliation_strings.search + publication window + has_doi) and a field projection; probe openalex_select_contract: HTTP 400 with the closed list of selectable field names. 12 anchor-selection requests, 0 failures.
historical_depth: Works from the 1800s to present. `created_date` gives per-work index history; the publication date itself is a mutable current value.
licence_note: OpenAlex states its data is released under CC0 1.0 Universal (https://openalex.org/licenses, 'All data ... is licensed under CC0 1.0'). Quoted from the licence page surfaced by the API's own meta.notice.
machine_interface: REST JSON, cursor paging, `select` field projection
name: OpenAlex
notes: Anonymous daily budget is a real ceiling: the API's meta.notice states requests share a $0.10/day budget per IP without a key, and that mailto does not raise it. A free key exists (POST https://api.openalex.org/api-keys with an email, then the emailed link must be clicked) but the click-through is a human step and was not attempted.
rate_policy: Documented: add `mailto` to join the polite pool. Observed in meta.notice: without an API key the request costs ~$0.001 against a $0.10/day shared budget per IP, so this workstream stayed at 12 requests and never paged deeply.
robots_summary: Not applicable: only the JSON API is touched, never HTML pages.
what_is_new: Definitional for the sample (60/60 anchors) and the only source here that exposes a per-work index-creation timestamp. Contributes the anchor universe, not de-duplication value.
